title.zh: 卷三十九 志第二十: 樂上 雅樂 散樂 鼓吹樂 本朝樂曲
title.en: Volume 39 Treatises 20: Music 1 - Formal Music, Court Music, Wind Instrument Music, Our Own Court Music
title.raw: 卷三十九 志第二十: 樂上 雅樂 散樂 鼓吹樂 本朝樂曲 Volume 39 Treatises 20: Music 1 - Formal Music, Court Music, Wind Instrument Music, Our Own Court Music

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「王者功成作樂，治定制禮。

translations.literal: The Classic says: "When a true king has achieved his meritorious work, he creates music; when order is established, he fixes ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says: "When a true king has completed his great work, he composes music; when governance is settled, he establishes ritual."

translations.literal: " Is this not the superfluous flourish of the Two Emperors and Three Kings!
translations.idiomatic: " Surely this is no mere ornamental excess of the Two Emperors and Three Kings!

sentences.zh: 蓋有天下者，將一軌度、正民俗、合人神、和上下，舍禮樂何以焉。

translations.literal: For those who possess the realm must unify standards, rectify custom, harmonize spirits and humans and upper and lower — apart from ritual and music, how could this be done?
translations.idiomatic: Whoever holds the realm must unify standards, set custom right, join spirits and humans, and harmonize high and low — without ritual and music, how could any of this be achieved?

sentences.zh: 金初得宋，始有金石之樂，然而未盡其美也。

translations.literal: When the Jin first obtained the Song, they first had metal-and-stone music, yet they had not yet attained its full excellence.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin first conquered the Song, they acquired bell-and-chime music for the first time, but its full refinement was still lacking.

sentences.zh: 及乎大定、明昌之際，日修月葺，粲然大備。

translations.literal: By the time of the Dading and Mingchang reigns, day by day they repaired and month by month they restored it, until it shone forth in full completeness.
translations.idiomatic: By the Dading and Mingchang eras, the court refined the system day by day and month by month until the musical establishment stood complete in splendid array.

sentences.zh: 其隸太常者，即郊廟、祀享、大宴、大朝會宮縣二舞是也。

translations.literal: That which was subordinate to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was precisely the palace ensemble and the two dances for suburban and temple sacrifices, sacrificial offerings, great banquets, and great court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Music under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices comprised the palace ensemble and the two ritual dances used at suburban and temple sacrifices, sacrificial offerings, great banquets, and major court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 隸教坊者，則有鐃歌鼓吹，天子行幸鹵簿導引之樂也。

translations.literal: That subordinate to the Music Bureau had gong songs and wind-and-drum music — the music that guided the emperor's procession when he went on tour.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Bureau oversaw gong songs and wind-and-drum ensembles — the music that led the imperial procession whenever the Son of Heaven traveled.

translations.literal: There was variety music.
translations.idiomatic: There was also variety music.

translations.literal: There was Bohai music.
translations.idiomatic: There was Bohai music as well.

sentences.zh: 有本國舊音，世宗嘗寫其意度為雅曲，史錄其一，其俚者弗載雲。

translations.literal: There were the old melodies of the native state; Emperor Shizong once set down their modes as formal music, and the histories record one of them; the vulgar ones are not recorded, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the old melodies of the Jin homeland. Emperor Shizong once transcribed their modes into formal court music; the histories preserve one such piece, while vulgar tunes were deliberately left unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年，詔用唐、宋故事，置所，講議禮樂。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Mingchang, an edict ordered that Tang and Song precedents be followed, an office was established, and ritual and music were discussed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Mingchang, the court decreed that Tang and Song precedents be followed, established an office, and convened discussions on ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 有司謂：「雅樂自周、漢以來止存大法，魏、晉而後更造律度，訖無定論。

translations.literal: The responsible officials said: "From Zhou and Han onward formal music preserved only the great principles; after Wei and Jin they repeatedly remade pitch standards, yet no final conclusion was ever reached."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials reported: "From Zhou and Han onward, formal music preserved only the broad principles; after Wei and Jin, courts repeatedly remade pitch standards, yet no lasting consensus was ever reached."

sentences.zh: 至後周保定中，得古玉鬥於地中，以造尺律，其後牛弘以為不可，止用蘇綽鐵尺，至隋亦用之。

translations.literal: In the Baoding era of Later Zhou, an ancient jade bushel measure was obtained from underground and used to make the foot-rule and pitch pipes; afterward Niu Hong held this impossible and used only Su Chuo's iron foot-rule, which the Sui also employed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoding era of Later Zhou, an ancient jade bushel measure was unearthed and used to derive the foot-rule and pitch pipes; later Niu Hong rejected this method, and courts used only Su Chuo's iron foot-rule — a standard the Sui dynasty also adopted.

sentences.zh: 唐興，因隋樂不改，及黃巢之亂，樂縣散失，太常博士殷盈孫以周法鑄穀鐘、編鐘，處士蕭承訓等校石磐，合而奏之。

translations.literal: When the Tang rose, they took over Sui music without change; at the turmoil of Huang Chao the musical stands were scattered and lost; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun cast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, and the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others tuned stone chimes, and together they were played.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang rose, they retained Sui music unchanged. During Huang Chao's rebellion the court instruments were scattered and lost. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun recast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, while the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others retuned stone chimes, and the restored ensemble was played together once more.

sentences.zh: 至周顯德以黍定律，議者謂比唐樂高五律。

translations.literal: In Later Zhou's Xiande reign pitch was set by millet grains; debaters said it was five notes higher than Tang music.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Zhou's Xiande reign, pitch was derived from millet grains; critics said the new standard stood five notes higher than Tang music.

sentences.zh: 宋初亦用王朴所制樂，時和峴以周顯德律音近哀思，乃依西京銅望臬、石尺重造十二管，取聲下王樸一律。

translations.literal: Early Song also used the music Wang Pu had made; at the time He Xian held that the Xiande pitch sounded too near grief and longing, so relying on the Western Capital's bronze pitch-standard and stone foot-rule he remade the twelve pipes, lowering the pitch one note below Wang Pu's.
translations.idiomatic: Early Song likewise used music composed by Wang Pu. He Xian argued that the Xiande pitch sounded too mournful, so he remade the twelve pipes according to the Western Capital's bronze pitch-standard and stone foot-rule, lowering the pitch one note below Wang Pu's standard.

sentences.zh: 景祐初，李照取黍累尺成律，以其聲猶高，更用太府布帛尺，遂下太常樂三律。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyou, Li Zhao took millet to stack up the foot-rule and make pitch pipes; because the sound was still high, he used instead the Grand Storehouse cloth-and-silk foot-rule, and thus lowered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices music by three notes.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingyou era, Li Zhao derived pitch pipes from a millet-based foot-rule; finding the tone still too high, he switched to the Grand Storehouse cloth-and-silk foot-rule and lowered Court of Imperial Sacrifices music by three notes.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，阮逸、胡瑗改造止下一律，或謂其聲弇鬱不和，依舊用王朴樂。

translations.literal: In Huangyou, Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan remade it, lowering only one note; some said the sound was muffled and gloomy and not harmonious, and they continued to use Wang Pu's music as before.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou, Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan revised the standard again, lowering it by only one note; some complained that the tone was muffled and discordant, so the court reverted to Wang Pu's music.

sentences.zh: 元豐間，楊傑參用李照鐘磬加四清聲，下王朴樂二律，以為新樂。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng period, Yang Jie drew on Li Zhao's bells and chimes, added four clear tones, lowered Wang Pu's music by two notes, and made this the new music.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanfeng, Yang Jie adapted Li Zhao's bells and chimes, added four clear tones, lowered Wang Pu's standard by two notes, and established this as the new court music.

sentences.zh: 元祐間，範鎮又造新律，下李照樂一律，而未用。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou period, Fan Zhen again made new pitch pipes, lowering Li Zhao's music by one note, yet it was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou, Fan Zhen devised yet another pitch standard, one note lower than Li Zhao's, but it was never adopted.

sentences.zh: 至崇甯間，魏漢津以範鎮知舊樂之高，無法以下之，乃以時君指節為尺，其所造鐘磐即今所用樂是也。

translations.literal: By the Chongning period, Wei Hanjin, seeing that Fan Zhen knew the old music was too high and had no way to lower it, took the reigning lord's finger joints as the foot-rule; the bells and chimes he made are precisely the music used today.
translations.idiomatic: By the Chongning era, Wei Hanjin recognized that Fan Zhen knew the old music was too high yet had no practical way to lower it, so he took the reigning emperor's finger joints as the foot-rule; the bells and chimes he cast are the instruments in use today.

sentences.zh: 然以王樸所制聲高，屢命改作，李照乙太府尺制律，人習舊聽疑於太重。

translations.literal: Yet because the music Wang Pu had made sounded high, the court repeatedly ordered revisions; Li Zhao followed the Grand Storehouse foot-rule to make pitch pipes, but people accustomed to the old sound suspected it was too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wang Pu's music sounded too high, the court repeatedly ordered revisions. Li Zhao followed the Grand Storehouse foot-rule to set pitch, but listeners accustomed to the old standard thought the new tone too low and dull.

sentences.zh: 其後范鎮等論樂，複用李照所用太府尺、即周、隋所用鐵尺，牛弘等以謂近古合宜者也。

translations.literal: Afterward Fan Zhen and others debated music and again used the Grand Storehouse foot-rule that Li Zhao had used — that is, the iron foot-rule used by Zhou and Sui — which Niu Hong and others held to be near antiquity and fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fan Zhen and others debated music and revived Li Zhao's Grand Storehouse foot-rule — the same iron standard used in Zhou and Sui times — which Niu Hong and others had regarded as close to antiquity and therefore appropriate.

sentences.zh: 今取見有樂，以唐初開元錢校其分寸亦同，則漢津所用指尺殆與周、隋、唐所用之尺同矣。

translations.literal: Now taking the music presently at hand and comparing its dimensions with early Tang Kaiyuan coins, they likewise agree; thus the finger-joint foot-rule Hanjin used was probably the same as the foot-rule used by Zhou, Sui, and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When the music now in use is measured against early Tang Kaiyuan coins, the dimensions match as well; Wei Hanjin's finger-joint foot-rule was therefore probably the same standard used in Zhou, Sui, and Tang times.

sentences.zh: 漢津用李照、範鎮之說，而恥同之，故用時君指節為尺，使眾人不敢輕議。

translations.literal: Hanjin used the theories of Li Zhao and Fan Zhen yet was ashamed to be identical with them, so he used the reigning lord's finger joints as the foot-rule to keep the multitude from lightly criticizing.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjin drew on Li Zhao's and Fan Zhen's theories yet was unwilling to appear merely to follow them, so he took the reigning emperor's finger joints as the foot-rule so that critics would not dismiss his work lightly.

sentences.zh: 其尺雖為詭說，其制乃與古同，而清濁高下皆適中，非出於法數之外私意妄為者也。

translations.literal: Although his foot-rule was a specious argument, its system was actually the same as antiquity, and clear and muddy, high and low, were all properly balanced — it was not something made by private whim outside the numerical laws.
translations.idiomatic: Although his foot-rule rested on a specious pretext, the resulting system matched antiquity, and its clear and muddy tones, high and low pitches, were all properly balanced — not the product of arbitrary private whim outside proper numerical standards.

sentences.zh: 蓋今之鐘磬雖崇寧之所制，亦周、隋、唐之樂也。

translations.literal: For today's bells and chimes, though made in Chongning, are also the music of Zhou, Sui, and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Thus today's bells and chimes, though cast in the Chongning era, are in substance the music of Zhou, Sui, and Tang.

sentences.zh: 閱今所用樂律，聲調和平，無太高太下之失，可以久用。

translations.literal: Examining the pitch pipes now in use, the tone is harmonious and peaceful, without the fault of being too high or too low, and they may be used for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the pitch standard now in use, the tone is harmonious and balanced, neither too high nor too low, and may be retained for long-term use.

sentences.zh: 唯辰鐘、辰磬自昔數缺，宜補鑄辰鐘十五，辰磬二十一，通舊各為二十四虡。

translations.literal: Only the chen bells and chen chimes have from old times been short in number; it is fitting to recast fifteen chen bells and twenty-one chen chimes, so that together with the old ones each set totals twenty-four stands.
translations.idiomatic: Only the chen bells and chen chimes have long been incomplete in number; the court should recast fifteen chen bells and twenty-one chen chimes so that, together with the old instruments, each set totals twenty-four stands.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「嘗觀宋人論樂，以為律主於人聲，不當泥於其器，要之在聲和而已。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I have observed Song discussions of music and hold that pitch pipes take their authority from the human voice; one should not be rigidly bound to the instruments — what matters is simply that the sound be harmonious."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "I have read Song debates on music and believe that pitch standards should follow the human voice rather than cling rigidly to instruments; what matters above all is harmonious sound."

sentences.zh: 」於是，命禮部符下南京，取宋舊工，更鑄辰鐘十有二。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered the Ministry of Rites to send orders down to Nanjing, take old Song craftsmen, and recast twelve chen bells.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered the Ministry of Rites to dispatch instructions to Nanjing, summon former Song craftsmen, and recast twelve chen bells.

sentences.zh: 又以舊鐘姑洗、夷則皆高五律，無射高二律，別鑄以補之，乃協。

translations.literal: Moreover, because the old bells for Guxian and Yize were each five notes too high and Wushe two notes too high, separate bells were cast to supplement them, and then they were in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Because the old Guxian and Yize bells were each five notes too high and the Wushe bell two notes too high, the court cast replacements to fill the gaps, and the ensemble came into harmony.

sentences.zh: 又琢辰磬各十有二，以其半少劣，擇其諧者而用之。

translations.literal: They also carved twelve chen chimes each; because about half were slightly inferior, they selected the harmonious ones for use.
translations.idiomatic: They also carved twelve chen chimes apiece; since roughly half were slightly inferior in tone, they selected the best-sounding pieces for use.

sentences.zh: 初，正隆間，海陵營太廟於汴，貞祐南遷，宣宗修之，以祔諸帝神主。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Zhenglong period, Prince Hailing built the Imperial Ancestral Temple at Bian; when Zhenyou moved south, Emperor Xuanzong repaired it to enshrine the spirit tablets of the various emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Zhenglong era, Prince Hailing built the Imperial Ancestral Temple at Bian. After the court moved south in the Zhenyou period, Emperor Xuanzong restored the temple to receive the spirit tablets of the former emperors.

sentences.zh: 其地，故宋景靈宮之址也。

translations.literal: The site was the former location of the Song Jingling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The site had been that of the Song dynasty's Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 掘其下，得編鐘十三，編磬八，皆刻「大晟」字。

translations.literal: When they dug beneath it, they obtained thirteen chime-bells and eight chime-stones, all inscribed with the characters "Dasheng."
translations.idiomatic: Excavation below the site yielded thirteen chime-bells and eight chime-stones, all inscribed with the mark "Dasheng."

sentences.zh: 時朝廷多故，禮器散亡，竟亦不能備也，

translations.literal: At the time the court had many troubles and ritual vessels were scattered and lost, and in the end they could not be made complete either,
translations.idiomatic: The court was then beset by many troubles, ritual vessels had been scattered and lost, and in the end the ensemble could not be made complete,

sentences.zh: 大定十一年，太常議：「按《唐會耍》舊制，南北郊宮縣用二十架，周、漢、魏、晉、宋、齊六朝及唐《開元》、宋《開寶禮》，其數皆同。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dading, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated: "According to the old system in the Tang Huiyao, the palace ensemble for the southern and northern suburban sacrifices used twenty stands; the six dynasties Zhou, Han, Wei, Jin, Song, and Qi, as well as the Tang Kaiyuan Rites and Song Kaibao Rites, all used the same number."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Dading, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "According to the Tang Huiyao, the palace ensemble for the southern and northern suburban sacrifices used twenty stands; Zhou, Han, Wei, Jin, Song, and Qi, as well as the Tang Kaiyuan Rites and Song Kaibao Rites, all prescribed the same number."

sentences.zh: 《宋會耍》用三十六架，《五禮新儀》用四十八架，其數多，似乎太侈。

translations.literal: The Song Huiyao used thirty-six stands and the Wuli Xinyi used forty-eight stands — their numbers were greater and seem excessively lavish.
translations.idiomatic: The Song Huiyao prescribed thirty-six stands and the Wuli Xinyi forty-eight — numbers that seem excessively lavish by comparison.

sentences.zh: 今擬《太常因革禮》，天子宮縣之樂三十六虡，宗廟與殿庭同，郊丘則二十虡，宜用宮縣二十架，登歌編鐘、編磬各一虡。

translations.literal: Now following the Taichang Yingeli, the Son of Heaven's palace ensemble music has thirty-six stands; the ancestral temple and palace hall are the same, while suburban mounds use twenty stands — it is fitting to use a palace ensemble of twenty stands, with elevated song, chime-bells, and chime-stones each one stand.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Taichang Yingeli, the Son of Heaven's palace ensemble comprises thirty-six stands for ancestral temple and palace hall alike, while suburban mounds use twenty — the court should therefore employ a palace ensemble of twenty stands, with elevated song, chime-bells, and chime-stones each occupying one stand.

sentences.zh: 又按《周禮大司樂》：'凡樂，圜鐘為宮，黃鐘為角，太蔟為徵，姑洗為羽。

translations.literal: Moreover, according to the Zhouli Director of Music: "In all music, the round bell serves as gong, huangzhong as jue, taicu as zhi, and guxian as yu."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhouli Director of Music also states: "In all music, the round bell serves as gong, huangzhong as jue, taicu as zhi, and guxian as yu."

sentences.zh: 雷鼓、雷鞀、孤竹之管、雲和之琴瑟、雲門之舞，冬日至於地上之圜丘奏之，若樂六變，則天神皆降，可得而禮矣。

translations.literal: Thunder drums, thunder tambourines, solitary bamboo pipes, Yunhe zithers, and the Yunmen dance — at the winter solstice they are performed at the round mound altar on earth; if the music undergoes six changes, then the heavenly spirits all descend and may be received in ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Thunder drums, thunder tambourines, solitary bamboo pipes, Yunhe zithers, and the Yunmen dance are performed at the round mound altar on the winter solstice; when the music undergoes six changes, the heavenly spirits descend and may be received in ritual."

translations.literal: "The six changes" means six completions.
translations.idiomatic: "Six changes" means six complete performances.

translations.literal: Tang and Song followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Song followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 蓋圜鐘，夾鐘也，用為宮者以上應房、心，有天帝明堂之象也。

translations.literal: For the round bell is jiazhong; used as gong, it corresponds above to the lodges Fang and Xin, having the image of the Heavenly Emperor's Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The round bell is jiazhong; employed as gong, it corresponds above to the lodges Fang and Xin and evokes the Bright Hall of the Heavenly Emperor.

sentences.zh: 宮聲三奏，角徵羽各一奏，合陽之奇數，欲神聽之也。

translations.literal: The gong tone is played three times, jue, zhi, and yu each once — combining the odd numbers of yang, intending that the spirits should hear.
translations.idiomatic: The gong tone is played three times, while jue, zhi, and yu are each played once — an odd-numbered pattern of yang tones meant to draw the spirits' attention.

sentences.zh: 凡樂起于陽，至少陰而止，圜鐘自卯至申其數有六，故六變而樂止，則天神皆降，可得而禮也。

translations.literal: All music begins in yang and stops at least yin; the round bell from mao to shen has the number six, therefore with six changes the music stops, and then the heavenly spirits all descend and may be received in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: All music begins in yang and ends at least yin; the round bell spans from mao to shen in six stages, so after six changes the music ceases, the heavenly spirits descend, and ritual reception becomes possible.

sentences.zh: 樂曲之名，唐以'和'，宋以'安'，本朝定樂曲以'甯'為名，今止有太廟祫享樂曲，而郊祀樂曲未備。

translations.literal: As for the names of musical pieces, Tang used "He," Song used "An," and our dynasty fixed musical pieces with "Ning" in the name; now there are only the Imperial Ancestral Temple joint-offering pieces, while suburban sacrifice pieces are not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: Tang named ritual pieces with "He," Song with "An," and our dynasty adopted "Ning"; at present only the Imperial Ancestral Temple joint-offering pieces exist, while suburban sacrifice pieces are still incomplete.

sentences.zh: 皇統九年拜天用《乾甯之曲》，今圜丘降神固可就用。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Huangtong, worship of Heaven used the "Qianning" piece; for the round mound's descent of the spirit it can certainly be used as is.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Huangtong, the worship of Heaven used the "Qianning" piece, which can certainly be reused for the round mound's descent-of-spirit rite.

sentences.zh: 今太廟祫享，皇帝升降行止奏《昌甯之曲》，迎俎奏《豐甯之曲》，酌獻、舞出入奏《肅甯之曲》，飲福奏《福甯之曲》，宋《開寶禮》亦可就用。

translations.literal: Now for the Imperial Ancestral Temple joint offering, when the emperor ascends, descends, moves, or stops, the "Changning" piece is played; for welcoming the offering stand the "Fengning" piece; for libation, offering, and dancers entering and leaving the "Suning" piece; for drinking the blessing the "Funing" piece — the Song Kaibao Rites may also be used as is.
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Ancestral Temple joint offering, the emperor's ascent, descent, movement, and pauses are accompanied by "Changning"; welcoming the offering stand by "Fengning"; libation, offering, and dancers' entry and exit by "Suning"; and drinking the blessing by "Funing" — pieces that may likewise be drawn from the Song Kaibao Rites.

sentences.zh: 余有郊祀曲名，皇帝入中濆、奠玉幣、迎俎、酌獻、舞出入樂曲，宜皆以'寧'字制名。

translations.literal: As for the remaining suburban sacrifice piece names — when the emperor enters the inner precinct, presents jade and silk, welcomes the offering stand, pours libations, and dancers enter and leave — all should be named with the character "Ning."
translations.idiomatic: The remaining suburban sacrifice pieces — for the emperor's entry to the inner precinct, presentation of jade and silk, welcoming the offering stand, libation, and dancers' entry and exit — should all be named with "Ning."

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered the Hanlin Academy to compose them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then ordered the Hanlin Academy to compose them.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入中濆奏《昌甯之曲》，降神、送神奏《乾甯之曲》，昊天上帝奏《洪甯之曲》，皇地祇奏《坤甯之曲》，配位奏《永甯之曲》，飲福奏《福甯之曲》，升降、望燎、出入大小次，並與入中濆同，餘載儀注及樂章。

translations.idiomatic: " The Director of Great Music struck the huangzhong bell; the five bells to the right answered in turn; "Changning" began to play, and the emperor emerged.

translations.idiomatic: After the amnesty had been read aloud, the officials performed the ritual dance. translations.idiomatic: On a jiayin day in the eleventh month of the second year of Mingchang, Emperor Zhangzong forbade actors from portraying emperors of past dynasties in jest or shouting "ten thousand years," imposing heavy penalties under the statute for impermissible conduct.

sentences.zh: 泰和初，有司又奏太常工人數少，即以渤海，漢人教坊及大興府樂人兼習以備用。

translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe era, officials again reported that Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians were too few, and assigned musicians from the Bohai and Han Music Bureaus and from Daxing Prefecture to train jointly as reserves.

translations.literal: On the gengshen day of the eleventh month of the ninth year of Dading under Emperor Shizong, on the crown prince's birthday the emperor banqueted at the Eastern Palace, ordered new music performed, and said to the ministers: "I composed this piece, named 'Joy of Ruler and Subject.' Now the realm is at peace — to share it with you, is this not joy?"

translations.literal: " Its text and melody are not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Its lyrics and melody have not been preserved.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月乙亥，上禦睿思殿，命歌者歌女直詞，顧謂皇太子曰：「朕思先朝所行之事，未嘗暫忘，故時聽此詞，亦欲令汝輩知女直醇質之風。

translations.literal: On the yihai day of the fourth month of the thirteenth year, the emperor attended the Ruisi Hall, ordered singers to sing Jurchen lyrics, turned and said to the crown prince: "I think of what the former court did and have never forgotten it even for a moment; therefore I often listen to these lyrics, and also wish to make you know the pure and plain style of the Jurchen."
translations.idiomatic: On a yihai day in the fourth month of the thirteenth year, the emperor attended the Ruisi Hall and ordered singers to perform Jurchen lyrics. Turning to the crown prince, he said: "I never forget, even for a moment, what the former court did; I listen to these songs often so that you too may know the plain and unadorned spirit of our Jurchen forebears."

sentences.zh: 至於文字、語言或不通曉，是忘本也！

translations.literal: As for writing and speech, if one does not understand them, that is forgetting one's roots!
translations.idiomatic: If you do not understand our script and language, you have forgotten your roots!

sentences.zh: 」二十五年四月，幸上京，宴宗室于皇武殿，飲酒樂，上諭之曰：「今日甚欲成醉，此樂不易得也。

translations.literal: " In the fourth month of the twenty-fifth year, he visited the Upper Capital, banqueted the imperial clan in the Huangwu Hall, drank and made merry; the emperor instructed them: "Today I very much wish to become fully drunk — this joy is not easily obtained."
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth month of the twenty-fifth year he visited the Upper Capital and banqueted the imperial clan in the Huangwu Hall. As they drank and rejoiced, he told them: "Today I mean to drink myself fully drunk — such joy does not come easily."

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖過故鄉，與父老歡飲，擊築而歌，令諸兒和之。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Gaozu of Han passed his old home, drank joyfully with the elders, struck the zhu and sang, and ordered his sons to join in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Emperor Gaozu of Han visited his old home, drank merrily with the local elders, struck the zhu and sang, and had his sons join in the chorus.

sentences.zh: 彼起布衣，尚且如是，況我祖宗世有此土，今天下一統，朕巡幸至此，何不樂飲！

translations.literal: He rose from common cloth and still acted thus — how much more so for us, whose ancestors for generations possessed this land; now the realm is unified, and I have come on tour to this place — why not drink in joy!
translations.idiomatic: He had risen from common cloth and still did as much — how much more should we rejoice, whose ancestors held this land for generations, and who now, with the realm unified, have come on tour to our homeland. Why should we not drink in joy!

sentences.zh: 」于時宗室婦女起舞，進酒畢，群臣故老起舞，上曰：「吾來故鄉數月矣，今回期已近，未嘗有一人歌本曲者，汝曹來前，吾為汝歌。

translations.literal: " At that time the women of the imperial clan danced; when wine had been presented, the ministers and old elders danced. The emperor said: "I have been in my old home several months; now the day of return is near, yet not one person has sung the native melody — come forward, all of you, and I will sing for you."
translations.idiomatic: " The women of the imperial clan danced, and after wine had been presented, the ministers and elders danced as well. The emperor said: "I have been in my homeland for months now, and our return is near, yet no one has sung the old native melody. Come forward — I shall sing it for you."

sentences.zh: 」乃命宗室子敘坐殿下者皆上殿，面聽上歌。

translations.literal: " He then ordered all the imperial clansmen seated in ranks below the hall to ascend the hall and face him to listen to his singing.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered all the imperial clansmen seated in ranks below the hall to come up and listen as he sang.

sentences.zh: 曲道祖宗創業艱難，及所以繼述之意。

translations.literal: The piece told of the ancestors' arduous founding of the enterprise and the meaning of how to carry it on.
translations.idiomatic: The song spoke of the hardships of the ancestors' founding and of the purpose of carrying their work forward.

sentences.zh: 上既自歌，至慨想祖宗音容如睹之語，悲感不復能成聲，歌畢，泣下數行。

translations.literal: When the emperor had sung himself and reached the words about vividly recalling the ancestors' countenance as if seen before him, grief overwhelmed him so he could no longer finish the sound; when the song was done, several streams of tears fell.
translations.idiomatic: As he sang and reached the lines recalling the ancestors' faces as though still before him, grief overwhelmed him and his voice broke. When the song ended, tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 右丞相元忠暨群臣宗戚捧觴上壽，皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The right chief minister Yuanzhong together with the ministers and imperial kin raised cups to offer longevity, all shouting "ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: The right chief minister Yuanzhong, together with the ministers and imperial kin, raised their cups to wish him long life, all shouting "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 於是諸老人更歌本曲，如私家相會，暢然歡洽。

translations.literal: Thereupon the old men again sang the native melody, like a private family gathering, freely and joyfully harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Then the elders sang the native melody again, as at a family gathering, in open and joyful harmony.

sentences.zh: 上複續調歌曲，留坐一更，極歡而罷。

translations.literal: The emperor again continued tuning and singing pieces, remained seated one watch of the night, and ended in utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sang on, and the company remained until the first watch of the night, ending in the fullest joy.

translations.literal: Its text says:
translations.idiomatic: The lyrics read:

translations.literal: Alas, our ancestor — sacred was Wuyuan!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, our ancestor — how sacred was Wuyuan!

translations.literal: He received the bright mandate; his merit shone upon Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He received the bright mandate, and his merit shone upon Heaven.

translations.literal: He saved the drowning and rescued the distressed, planting deep roots and firm bonds.
translations.idiomatic: He rescued the drowning and the desperate, planting deep roots and firm bonds.

translations.literal: He opened the way for our posterity and transmitted blessings for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the way for our posterity and passed down blessings for ten thousand generations.

translations.literal: Woe to Hailing of the River — licentious, dim-witted, guilty of many crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Woe to Prince Hailing — licentious and benighted, guilty of countless crimes.

translations.literal: He reversed Heaven's way and tormented the realm within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: He reversed Heaven's way and brought torment to the realm.

translations.literal: From the founding of old down to succession of the body.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of old down to the succession of the throne.

translations.literal: The accumulated enterprise was about to sink together and fall.
translations.idiomatic: The accumulated enterprise was on the verge of ruin.

translations.literal: All looked to where the mandate leaned; none consulted for agreement.
translations.idiomatic: All eyes turned to where the mandate leaned, without seeking anyone's consent.

translations.literal: The ancestral temple was of utmost weight; human hearts were hard to refuse.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple weighed above all else, and human hearts could not refuse.

translations.literal: Reluctantly matching joyful advancement, I extended my succession.
translations.idiomatic: Reluctantly accepting joyful advancement, I took up the succession.

translations.literal: Twenty-four years, diligent in the ten thousand affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty-four years I have been diligent in the ten thousand affairs of state.

translations.literal: Hundreds of millions of common folk harbor peace and security.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of millions of common people live in peace and security.

translations.literal: The state is at leisure, broadly without affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The state is at ease, broadly free of trouble.

translations.literal: Thus I turn affection to the Upper Capital, the founding emperor's domain.
translations.idiomatic: Thus my heart turns to the Upper Capital, the founding emperor's domain.

translations.literal: Now that I have come on this tour, sorrowfully I reflect.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have come on this tour, sorrow fills my thoughts.

translations.literal: Scenes and things have diminished and wasted — scarcely as in former times.
translations.idiomatic: The land and its sights have faded — scarcely what they once were.

translations.literal: In village and in hamlet, none are as at the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: In every village and hamlet, nothing remains as it was at the beginning.

translations.literal: Although not as at the beginning, I myself delight in this.
translations.idiomatic: Though it is no longer as at the beginning, I take joy in it nonetheless.

translations.literal: Although not as in former times, I view it without difference.
translations.idiomatic: Though it is not as in former times, I behold it without estrangement.

translations.literal: Gazing fondly and sighing in thought upon the ancestors' old halls.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing fondly and sighing, I think of the ancestors' old halls.

translations.literal: Their voices and countenances, connected and connected, seem exactly as if seen.
translations.idiomatic: Their voices and faces return again and again, as though I could see them still.

translations.literal: Childhood play and youthful longing — each place stands out clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Childhood play and youthful longing — each place stands clear in memory.

translations.literal: In the strong years I passed through them; suddenly it seems as of old.
translations.idiomatic: The paths I walked in my prime seem suddenly as they once were.

translations.literal: Companions of old years in travel — dimly, dimly as yesterday.
translations.idiomatic: Companions of years past seem near again, as though it were only yesterday.

translations.literal: Joy and earnest parting — as if morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Joy and earnest parting feel as close as morning and evening.

translations.literal: Alas for long separation — how is it that we are not joyful?
translations.idiomatic: Alas for this long parting — how can we fail to rejoice?

translations.literal: Suburban sacrifice hymn texts.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns for Suburban Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入中濆，宮縣黃鐘宮《昌甯之曲》：凡步武同。

translations.literal: The emperor enters the central mound; the palace ensemble plays in Yellow Bell mode, "Prospering Tranquility" — all paces and bearing are alike.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor enters the central mound, the palace ensemble sounds the Yellow Bell mode, "Prospering Tranquility"; every pace and bearing match the prescribed pattern.

translations.literal: In dark ceremonial robes, solemn and stately, he draws near the central mound.
translations.idiomatic: Robed in dark ceremonial vestments, solemn and still, he approaches the central mound.

translations.literal: Gazing upon the round altar — august is the Heavenly Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Behold the round altar — how august the Heavenly Sovereign on high.

translations.literal: The spirit-sacrifice is first proclaimed; bell-tone and fragrance are virtue's substance.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit-sacrifice begins; bell-tones and fragrance rise as offerings of virtue.

translations.literal: Thereupon reaching the hundred spirits — they brightly receive their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Thus it reaches the hundred spirits, who brightly take up their appointed offices.

sentences.zh: 降神，宮縣《乾甯之曲》、《仁豐道洽之舞》。

translations.literal: Escorting the spirits downward: palace ensemble, "Heavenly Tranquility," dance "Benevolence Abundant, the Way Harmonized."
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the spirits down: the palace ensemble plays "Heavenly Tranquility" and the dance "Benevolence Abundant, the Way in Harmony."

sentences.zh: 圜鐘為宮，黃鐘為角，太蔟為徵，姑洗為羽。

translations.literal: Round bells as tonic, yellow bell as second, great cluster as third, maiden wash as fifth.
translations.idiomatic: The round bells serve as tonic, yellow bell as second, great cluster as third degree, and maiden wash as fifth.

translations.idiomatic: The round bells are played thrice; yellow bell, great cluster, and maiden wash each once — the words are the same:

translations.literal: Our Jin's rising — August Heaven bestows favor.
translations.idiomatic: As our Jin dynasty arose, August Heaven granted its blessing.

translations.literal: Only the spirits' blessing — here at this suburban manifestation.
translations.idiomatic: By the spirits' favor alone we make this suburban appearance.

translations.literal: There is jade for the ritual; there are victims for the offering.
translations.idiomatic: Jade for the rites, victims for the offering.

translations.literal: About to receive its brilliance — come in peace, come in feast.
translations.idiomatic: Soon to receive its radiance — come in peace, come to feast.

sentences.zh: 皇帝盥洗，宮縣黃鐘宮《昌甯之曲》：

translations.literal: The emperor washes hands; palace ensemble, Yellow Bell mode, "Prospering Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: The emperor performs the hand-washing; the palace ensemble plays in Yellow Bell mode, "Prospering Tranquility":

translations.literal: Following Heaven to serve Heaven; honoring the ancestral temple in carrying out rites.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Heaven through Heaven, he honors the ancestral temple and prepares the rite.

translations.literal: Thereupon ordering the responsible officials, presenting the timely urn and basin.
translations.idiomatic: He charges the officers in charge to present the urn and basin at the appointed hour.

translations.literal: Drawing from that, pouring into this — then ascending the altar steps.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing water there and pouring it here, he ascends the altar steps.

translations.literal: Before the affair, devout; the spirits' toil is gentle and kind.
translations.idiomatic: Devout before the rite begins — the spirits' kindly labor brings ease.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升壇，登歌大呂宮《昌甯之曲》：

translations.literal: The emperor ascends the altar; ascent songs, great Yü mode, "Prospering Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascends the altar; the ascent singers perform in great Yü mode, "Prospering Tranquility":

translations.literal: The altar stands in the state's south — lofty, lofty its base.
translations.idiomatic: The altar stands south of the capital, its footings rising high and grand.

translations.literal: How abundant the august king — at this time he arrives and halts.
translations.idiomatic: How august the sovereign — at this hour he takes his stand.

translations.literal: Utmost sincerity penetrates the spirits; he can perform spirit-sacrifice and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Utmost sincerity reaches the spirits; he worthily performs the spirit-sacrifice and offering.

translations.literal: For ten thousand years — August Heaven's son.
translations.idiomatic: For myriad years — son of August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 昊天上帝，奠玉幣，登歌大呂宮《洪甯之曲》：

translations.literal: August Heaven the Supreme Lord, laying jade and silk; ascent songs, great Yü mode, "Great Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: To August Heaven the Supreme Lord, offering jade and silks — ascent songs in great Yü mode, "Great Tranquility":

translations.literal: Solemn, solemn the king and lord — he has severity and has support.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn and still is the king and lord — dignified in bearing, well attended.

translations.literal: His belt pendants ring clear; the round altar is what he ascends.
translations.idiomatic: His belt pendants chime as he climbs the round altar.

translations.literal: Fine virtue rises and is heard; fragrance is not from millet and sacrificial grain.
translations.idiomatic: His fine virtue rises to be heard — the fragrance lies not in grain alone.

translations.literal: The High Bright descends to oversee; the hundred spirits receive their posts.
translations.idiomatic: The High Bright One descends to watch; the hundred spirits take their offices.

translations.literal: Imperial Earth Spirit, "Earthly Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: To the Imperial Earth Spirit — "Earthly Tranquility":

translations.literal: Solemn and reverent toward the clear spirit; personally performing the laid offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn and reverent toward the clear Earth Spirit, he personally lays the offerings.

translations.literal: What are its offerings?
translations.idiomatic: What offerings are presented?

translations.literal: Yellow jade cube and fashioned silks.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow jade cube and fashioned silks.

translations.literal: The attendant-sacrificed host of spirits — all ordered in their places.
translations.idiomatic: The host of spirits in attendance — each ranks in its proper place.

translations.literal: Only the sovereign can feast them; truly gathered is the bright affair.
translations.idiomatic: Only the sovereign can receive them; the glorious rite is truly gathered complete.

sentences.zh: 配位太祖皇帝，《永甯之曲》：

translations.literal: The paired seat: Grand Ancestor Emperor, "Eternal Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: For the paired seat of Grand Ancestor Emperor — "Eternal Tranquility":

translations.literal: First raising the bright spirit-sacrifice — August Heaven, Queen Earth.
translations.idiomatic: He first lifts the bright spirit-sacrifice to August Heaven and Queen Earth.

translations.literal: Imperial ancestor Wuyuan — thereupon made spirit-lord.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial ancestor Wuyuan, now set as spirit-lord of the rite.

translations.literal: Merit displayed in aged peace — sung to great Yü.
translations.idiomatic: His merit shines in settled elder peace — hymned in great Yü mode.

translations.literal: To settle our thoughts accomplished — rank upon rank this blessing.
translations.idiomatic: To settle our thoughts in fulfillment — blessings heaped rank on rank.

sentences.zh: 司徒迎俎，宮縣黃鐘宮《豐甯之曲》：

translations.literal: Minister of Works welcomes the offering stand; palace ensemble, Yellow Bell mode, "Abundant Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works receives the offering stand; the palace ensemble plays Yellow Bell mode, "Abundant Tranquility":

translations.literal: Solemn, august — the Son of Heaven personally sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn and august, the Son of Heaven performs the sacrifice in person.

translations.literal: The host of ministers assist him — none without reverent stillness.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers assist him — none without reverent devotion.

translations.literal: Offering stands and vessels all displayed — the things are excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Stands and vessels are fully set forth — how fine the offerings.

translations.literal: Fragrant aroma first rises — the bright spirits feast in joy.
translations.idiomatic: Fragrant smoke first ascends — the bright spirits feast and rejoice.

sentences.zh: 昊天上帝，酌獻，登歌大呂宮《嘉甯之曲》：

translations.literal: August Heaven the Supreme Lord, libation offering; ascent songs, great Yü mode, "Fine Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: To August Heaven the Supreme Lord — libation offering — ascent songs in great Yü mode, "Fine Tranquility":

translations.literal: Suburban spirit-sacrifice displays reverence; illuminating service to the upper spirits.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban spirit-sacrifice reverence is shown — brightly serving the spirits on high.

translations.literal: The great wine-vessel on the mat — there is strained wine, its fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: The great wine-jar rests on the mat; strained wine, how fragrant.

translations.literal: Pouring as one offers it — may the spirits drink their fill and halt.
translations.idiomatic: We pour and offer it — may the spirits drink their fill.

translations.literal: Fortune and emolument come fittingly, to answer the bright sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and blessing come as fitting return for the bright sacrifice.

translations.literal: Imperial Earth Spirit, "Great Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: To the Imperial Earth Spirit — "Great Tranquility":

translations.literal: Dark robes solemn, drawing near that great earth-altar.
translations.idiomatic: In dark ceremonial robes, solemn and still, he approaches the great earth-altar.

translations.literal: How bright the spirit shrine — burying silks, interring blood.
translations.idiomatic: How brightly shines the spirit shrine — silks are buried, blood is interred.

translations.literal: Thereupon raising the gourd cup, pouring words to offer the clean.
translations.idiomatic: He raises the gourd cup and pours the clean offering.

translations.literal: The square earth-carrier ever tranquil — upholding our imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: May the square earth realm ever rest in peace and uphold our imperial work.

sentences.zh: 配位太祖皇帝，《燕甯之曲》：、

translations.literal: Paired seat: Grand Ancestor Emperor, "Feasting Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: For the paired seat of Grand Ancestor Emperor — "Feasting Tranquility":

translations.literal: How abundant the lofty ancestress — first opening the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: How august the lofty ancestress — who first laid the great foundation.

translations.literal: Merit joins with Heaven; paired with Heaven to be exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Her merit joins Heaven's — matched with Heaven and exalted.

translations.literal: Offering at the season's clear essence — greatly solemn its observance.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings of the season's pure essence — how solemn the ceremony.

translations.literal: Come in peace, come in feast — fortune and emolument settle upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Come in peace, come to feast — fortune and blessing are settled upon them.

sentences.zh: 文舞退，武舞進，宮縣黃鐘宮《咸甯之曲》：

translations.literal: Civil dance withdraws, martial dance advances; palace ensemble, Yellow Bell mode, "Universal Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: The civil dance withdraws and the martial dance advances; the palace ensemble plays Yellow Bell mode, "Universal Tranquility":

translations.literal: Performing sacrifice at the suburban mound — "Cloud Gate" transformation dance.
translations.idiomatic: Offering sacrifice at the suburban mound — the transformed dance of "Cloud Gate."

translations.literal: Advancing, grasping vermilion staffs; stopping, waving pheasant plumes.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing with vermilion staffs in hand; halting, waving pheasant-feather plumes.

translations.literal: How bright the sagely culture — again resembling the holy martial.
translations.idiomatic: How brightly shines the sage culture — echoing the holy martial once more.

translations.literal: Without boundary is the merit — the Son of Heaven receives blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Boundless is the merit — the Son of Heaven receives Heaven's grace.

sentences.zh: 亞終獻，宮縣黃鐘宮《咸甯之曲》、《功成治定之舞》：

translations.literal: Second and final offerings; palace ensemble, Yellow Bell mode, "Universal Tranquility," dance "Merit Accomplished, Order Settled":
translations.idiomatic: The second and final offerings — palace ensemble in Yellow Bell mode, "Universal Tranquility," and the dance "Merit Accomplished, Order Settled":

sentences.zh: 掃地南郊，天神以俟，于皇君王，克禋克祀。

translations.literal: Sweeping the ground at the southern suburb, Heaven's spirits thereby wait; how august the king and lord — he can perform spirit-sacrifice and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The southern suburb is swept clean; Heaven's spirits await — how august the sovereign, worthily performing spirit-sacrifice and offering.

translations.literal: Exchanging with the spirits bright; dark wine in earthenware.
translations.idiomatic: He communes with the spirits — dark wine in earthen vessels.

translations.literal: Sincere mind tranquil and pure — not valuing flavors of food.
translations.idiomatic: The heart is sincere, still, and pure — the rite values not rich flavors.

sentences.zh: 皇帝飲福，登歌大呂宮《福甯之曲》：

translations.literal: The emperor drinks blessing; ascent songs, great Yü mode, "Blessing Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: The emperor partakes of the blessing-wine — ascent songs in great Yü mode, "Blessing Tranquility":

translations.literal: That by which one receives Heaven — nothing surpasses simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: To receive Heaven's mandate, nothing exceeds simplicity.

translations.literal: Heaven will bless it — only refinement, only unity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven blesses him — in refinement and singleness of purpose alone.

translations.literal: The great vessel thereupon drawn — fragrant aroma offering virtue.
translations.idiomatic: From the great wine-jar he pours — fragrance offering up virtue.

translations.literal: Favor us without boundary — descendants by the billion.
translations.idiomatic: Favor us without end — sons and grandsons beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 徹豆，登歌大呂宮《豐甯之曲》：

translations.literal: Removing the vessels; ascent songs, great Yü mode, "Abundant Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: The vessels are removed — ascent songs in great Yü mode, "Abundant Tranquility":

translations.literal: The great rite thereupon displayed — the vessels for offerings greatly ample.
translations.idiomatic: The great rite is now set forth — the offering vessels ample and full.

translations.literal: Solemn, solemn their bearing — how manifest the hundred lords.
translations.idiomatic: Grave and orderly their bearing — how glorious the host of lords.

translations.literal: The august numen descends to oversee; fragrance heard lies in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The august spirits descend to watch — fragrance is heard in virtue alone.

translations.literal: The bright spirit-sacrifice is thereby accomplished — good faith and felicity without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The bright spirit-sacrifice stands complete — blessing and joy without bound.

sentences.zh: 送神，宮縣圜鐘宮《乾甯之曲》：

translations.literal: Escorting the spirits away; palace ensemble, round-bell mode, "Heavenly Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the spirits away — the palace ensemble plays in round-bell mode, "Heavenly Tranquility":

translations.literal: Splendid, splendid Supreme Lord — overseeing the spirit-sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid and bright the Supreme Lord — overseeing the spirit-sacrifice.

translations.literal: Securely, solemnly they come to savor — brightly answering ancestor and paired spirit.
translations.idiomatic: They came to partake in solemn presence — brightly answering ancestor and consort.

translations.literal: The round altar four tiers complete — spirits rest in their places.
translations.idiomatic: The round altar stands complete in four tiers — the spirits rest in their places.

translations.literal: Ascent songs praise the send-off — Heaven's people joyful and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent songs praise the farewell — Heaven and humanity rejoice together.

translations.literal: Square-mound altar hymn texts.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns for the Square-Mound Altar.

translations.literal: Welcoming the spirits — "Supreme Tranquility."
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the spirits — "Supreme Tranquility."

sentences.zh: 大鐘宮再奏，太蔟角再奏，姑洗徵再奏，南呂羽再奏，詞同：

translations.literal: Great bell mode twice performed, great cluster second twice, maiden wash third twice, southern Yü fifth twice — texts alike:
translations.idiomatic: Great bell as tonic played twice, great cluster as second twice, maiden wash as third twice, southern Yü as fifth twice — the words are the same:

translations.literal: How utmost the Kun trigram's form — ten thousand things rely on it for life.
translations.idiomatic: Utmost is the form of Earth — the myriad beings live by its sustenance.

translations.literal: Weighing things, evenly bestowing — flowing humility, transforming fullness.
translations.idiomatic: It measures each thing and grants evenly — humility flows forth and fullness is transformed.

translations.literal: Rites perfected at the great earth-altar — sacrifice utmost in pure sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Rites are perfected at the great earth-altar — sacrifice in utmost sincerity.

translations.literal: August, august the spirit's regard — forever settling the realm within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: August is the spirits' favor — forever securing the realm within the four seas.

sentences.zh: 初獻盥洗，太蔟宮《肅甯之曲》：

translations.literal: First offering hand-washing; great cluster mode, "Solemn Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: First offering — hand-washing — in great cluster mode, "Solemn Tranquility":

translations.literal: Rites have five classics — none precedes sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Among the five classics of ritual, none comes before the rites of sacrifice.

translations.literal: At once extending sincerity — only at the proper time hand-washing.
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity is offered forthwith; hand-washing comes only at the appointed hour.

translations.literal: Each thing auspiciously purified — bearing and observance orderly and full.
translations.idiomatic: Every offering is purified for the rite; bearing and ceremony stand grave and complete.

translations.literal: Bestowing upon them pure blessing — come to savor, harmonious and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Grant them pure blessing; come to partake in harmony and gentle grace.

sentences.zh: 初獻升壇，應鐘宮《肅甯之曲》：

translations.literal: First offering ascends the altar; response-bell mode, "Solemn Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: First offering — ascent to the altar — in response-bell mode, "Solemn Tranquility":

translations.literal: Boundless virtue — how utmost the Kun origin!
translations.idiomatic: Boundless is its virtue — utmost is the origin of Earth!

translations.literal: Submerged yet firm in overcoming — sustaining life, truly abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Latent yet firm in strength, it sustains all life in true abundance.

translations.literal: The square-mound altar's observance — only reverence, no ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The rite at the square-mound altar honors reverence alone, not display.

translations.literal: May the spirits come! — timely savor, abundant offering.
translations.idiomatic: May the spirits come — in season they savor the ample offering.

sentences.zh: 初獻奠玉幣，太蔟宮《億甯之曲》：

translations.literal: First offering presents jade and silks; great cluster mode, "Abundant Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: First offering — presentation of jade and silks — in great cluster mode, "Abundant Tranquility":

translations.literal: Rites performed at the square marsh-altar — regalia and vessels fully displayed.
translations.idiomatic: The rite proceeds at the square marsh-altar; regalia and vessels are fully set forth.

translations.literal: Only the august Imperial Earth Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: To the august Imperial Earth Spirit alone.

translations.literal: Brightly summoned, they descend.
translations.idiomatic: Brightly summoned, the spirits descend.

translations.literal: Offering and burying jade and silks — pure sincerity shown within.
translations.idiomatic: Jade and silks are offered and buried; pure sincerity dwells within.

translations.literal: The spirits guard and enjoy — ascending and descending, this blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The spirits guard and partake; in their going and coming, blessing is bestowed.

sentences.zh: 司徒捧俎，太蔟宮《豐甯之曲》：

translations.literal: Minister of Works bears the offering stand; great cluster mode, "Abundant Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works bears the offering stand — in great cluster mode, "Abundant Tranquility":

translations.literal: Four tiers, ordered observance — altar at the square marsh-altar.
translations.idiomatic: Four tiers in ordered ceremony — the altar stands at the square marsh-altar.

translations.literal: Brightly serving the august Earth Spirit — facing yin upon the earthen mound.
translations.idiomatic: Brightly serving the august Earth Spirit — facing the north upon the earthen altar.

translations.literal: Pure offerings displayed at the side-altar — greatly excellent and ample.
translations.idiomatic: Pure offerings are set at the side-altar — how excellent and how full.

translations.literal: May the spirits bless it — like so many, like the rite.
translations.idiomatic: May the spirits bless it — in number and in form as the rite prescribes.

sentences.zh: 正位酌獻，太蔟宮《溥甯之曲》：

translations.literal: Principal seat, libation offering; great cluster mode, "Broad Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: Principal seat — libation offering — in great cluster mode, "Broad Tranquility":

translations.literal: Vast, vast the Kun virtue — nothing it does not bear.
translations.idiomatic: Vast is the virtue of Earth — nothing lies outside its bearing.

translations.literal: Yielding, compliant, advantageous, steadfast — embracing greatness, vast brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Yielding and compliant, firm and steadfast — it embraces greatness and vast light.

translations.literal: Stands and vessels already displayed — metal and stone are there.
translations.idiomatic: Stands and vessels stand arrayed; bells and chimes are in their place.

translations.literal: Within the four seas everlasting peace — fortune and emolument therein conferred.
translations.idiomatic: May the four seas know lasting peace — fortune and blessing bestowed therein.

sentences.zh: 配位酌獻配太宗也，太蔟宮《保甯之曲》：

translations.literal: Paired seat libation offering — paired with Grand Ancestor Taizong; great cluster mode, "Preserving Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: Paired seat — libation offering to Grand Ancestor Taizong — in great cluster mode, "Preserving Tranquility":

translations.literal: Text lacuna.
translations.idiomatic: The hymn text is missing.

sentences.zh: 亞終獻升壇，太蔟宮《咸甯之曲》：

translations.literal: Secondary and final offering ascends the altar; great cluster mode, "All-Pervading Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: Secondary and final offering — ascent to the altar — in great cluster mode, "All-Pervading Tranquility":

translations.literal: Lofty that fine altar — presenting jade at the square marsh-altar.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty stands that fine altar — jade is offered at the square marsh-altar.

translations.literal: The hundred lords reverently solemn — eight tones purely performed.
translations.idiomatic: The host of lords stand in reverent order; the eight tones ring pure and clear.

translations.literal: Sacrificial affairs brightly accomplished — yielding earth spirits moved and received.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrifice shines complete; the yielding earth spirits are moved and descend.

translations.literal: Removing the vessels; response-bell mode, "Abundant Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: The vessels are removed — in response-bell mode, "Abundant Tranquility":

translations.literal: Preparing the square-mound altar — auspicious purification is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The square-mound altar is made ready; auspicious purification is meet.

translations.literal: Stands and vessels tranquil and excellent — presented to the officials in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Stands and vessels rest still and fine; offerings are set before the presiding officers.

translations.literal: Rich, rich fragrant aroma — come to feast, come in observance.
translations.idiomatic: Fragrance rises rich and full — come to feast, come in due observance.

translations.literal: The suburban rite nears its end — sound and song carry the removal through.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban rite draws near its close; music and song accompany the withdrawal.

translations.literal: Escorting the spirits away; forest-bell mode, "Pacifying Tranquility":
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the spirits away — in forest-bell mode, "Pacifying Tranquility":

translations.literal: Following the earth's square mound — orderly and full, many observances.
translations.idiomatic: By the earth's square-mound altar — observances stand grave, full, and many.

translations.literal: Music completed in eight changes — numen and earth spirits descend in thought.
translations.idiomatic: Music completes its eight changes; spirits and earth deities descend in presence.

translations.literal: Offering remainder, removing vessels — divine gift brightly bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings are cleared and vessels withdrawn; the spirits' gift shines forth.

translations.literal: By the billion such years — forever blessing the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: For ten thousand ages — may the great foundation be blessed forever.

sentences.zh: 詣望燎位，太蔟宮《肅甯之曲》。

translations.literal: Proceeding to the sighting-burn position; great cluster mode, "Solemn Tranquility."
translations.idiomatic: Proceeding to the sighting-burn position — in great cluster mode, "Solemn Tranquility."

translations.literal: Text same as ascending the altar.
translations.idiomatic: The words are the same as for ascending the altar.
